chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from the one he mentioned, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the people of Syria came to him and said: 'I am a man versed in theology (kalam), jurisprudence, and the laws of inheritance, and I have come to debate with your companions.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is your speech from the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), or from yourself?' He said: 'From the words of the Messenger of God and from myself.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Then you are a partner of the Messenger of God.' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you have heard the revelation from God, the Mighty and Majestic, informing you?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Is obedience to you then obligatory just as obedience to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is obligatory?' He said: 'No.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) turned toward me and said: 'O Yunus ibn Yaqub! This one has already defeated himself before he even spoke.' Then he said: 'O Yunus! If you were skilled in theological debate, you would have spoken to him.' Yunus said: 'Alas, what a cause for regret!' I said: 'May I be your ransom! I heard you forbidding theological disputation and saying: Woe upon the companions of kalam who say: this is logically consistent and this is not, and this follows and this does not, and this we understand and this we do not.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I only said: Woe upon them if they abandon what I say and go toward what they desire.'

Then he said to me: 'Go out to the door and look at whoever you see from the theologians and bring him in.' He said: So I brought in Humran ibn Ayn, and he was skilled in theological speech, and I brought in al-Ahwal, and he was skilled in theological speech, and I brought in Hisham ibn Salim, and he was skilled in theological speech, and I brought in Qays ibn al-Masir — and in my estimation he was the best of them in theological speech — and he had learned the discipline of kalam from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

When the gathering had settled and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — who before the Hajj season used to settle for some days in a mountain at the edge of the sacred precinct in a tent pitched for him — brought his head out of his tent, there was a camel trotting. He said: 'Hisham! By the Lord of the Ka'ba!' We thought he meant a man from the descendants of Aqil of whom he had intense love. But it was Hisham ibn al-Hakam who arrived — the first whiskers of his beard just beginning to grow — and there was no one among us except those older than him in age. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) made room for him and said: 'Our helper with his heart, his tongue, and his hand.'

Then he said: 'O Humran! Speak to the man.' So he spoke to him and Humran prevailed over him. Then he said: 'O Taqi! Speak to him.' So he spoke to him and al-Ahwal prevailed over him. Then he said: 'O Hisham ibn Salim! Speak to him.' So they were evenly matched. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Qays al-Masir: 'Speak to him.' So he spoke to him, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) began to laugh at their exchange — at what had struck the Syrian — and said to the Syrian: 'Speak to this young man,' meaning Hisham ibn al-Hakam. He said: 'Yes.'

So he said to Hisham: 'O young man! Ask me about the Imamate of this one.' Hisham became so angry that he trembled, then said to the Syrian: 'O you! Is your Lord more watchful over His creation, or is creation watchful over itself?' The Syrian said: 'Rather, my Lord is more watchful over His creation.' He said: 'So what has He done with His watchfulness over them?' He said: 'He established for them a proof and a guide, so that they would not scatter or differ — one who unites them and rectifies their condition and informs them of their Lord's ordinances.' He said: 'So who is he?' He said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).' Hisham said: 'So after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'The Book and the Sunnah.' Hisham said: 'Have the Book and the Sunnah benefited us today in resolving our differences?' The Syrian said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then why are you and I differing, such that you came to us from Syria in opposition to us?'

He (the narrator) said: The Syrian fell silent. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to the Syrian: 'What is wrong with you that you do not speak?' The Syrian said: 'If I say we have not differed, I lie; and if I say that the Book and the Sunnah resolve our differences, that is invalid, because they both admit multiple interpretations; and if I say that we have differed and each of us claims to be upon the truth, then the Book and the Sunnah have not benefited us — except that I still have this argument over him.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask him — you will find him well-furnished.' So the Syrian said: 'O you! Who is more watchful over creation — their Lord or they themselves?' So Hisham said: 'Their Lord is more watchful over them than they are over themselves.' So the Syrian said: 'Has He then established for them one who gathers their word in unison, and rectifies their condition, and informs them of their right from their wrong?' Hisham said: 'During the time of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), or at this moment?' The Syrian said: 'During the time of the Messenger of God it was the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and at this moment — who?' So Hisham said: 'This one sitting here, to whom riders travel, and who informs us with the news of heaven and earth, an inheritance from father to grandfather.'

The Syrian said: 'How can I know that?' Hisham said: 'Ask him whatever comes to your mind.' The Syrian said: 'You have cut off my excuse — it is upon me to ask.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Syrian! I will inform you how your journey was, and how your travel route was — it was thus and so.' The Syrian turned to him saying, 'You speak the truth! I submit to God this very moment.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, you have believed in God this very moment. Islam comes before iman, and upon it (Islam) they inherit from each other and marry; and iman is that upon which they are rewarded.'

So the Syrian said: 'You speak the truth. So I now testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and that you are the successor of the successors.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) turned toward Humran and said: 'You conduct the speech according to the narrations and you are correct.' And he turned toward Hisham ibn Salim and said: 'You seek the narrations but you do not fully recognize them.' Then he turned toward al-Ahwal and said: 'You are an evasive analogist — you break one falsehood with another, except that your falsehood is more apparent.' Then he turned toward Qays al-Masir and said: 'You speak, and the closer you come to relating the hadith from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), the further you actually are from him. You mix truth with falsehood, and a little truth is sufficient against much falsehood. You and al-Ahwal are both agile deflectors.' Yunus said: 'By God, I thought he would say to Hisham something close to what he said to them.' Then he said: 'O Hisham! You almost never fall — you twist your legs; when you are about to touch the ground, you take flight. The likes of you should speak to the people. But beware of slipping — and intercession will follow it, God willing.'

key_terms.إِمَامَة: Imamate — the doctrine of divinely appointed leadership of the Muslim community after the Prophet
key_terms.الزَّلَّة: Slip, error (especially in speech or argument)
key_terms.الْأَثَر: Narration, transmitted report (from the Prophet or Imams)
key_terms.الْإِسْلَام: Submission (the outward dimension of faith, including acts of worship and social law)
key_terms.الْإِيمَان: Iman — the inner dimension of faith (conviction, belief)
key_terms.وَصِيُّ الْأَوْصِيَاء: Successor of the successors — reference to the Imam's position in the line of divinely appointed leaders

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia argument for the necessity of the Imam after the Prophet?
ai.summary: This lengthy narrative recounts a historical encounter near Mecca before the Hajj season, where Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) orchestrated a theological debate between a Syrian scholar and his own companions, culminating in Hisham ibn al-Hakam's brilliant defense of the Imamate. The Imam demonstrated that the Book and Sunnah alone cannot resolve doctrinal disputes without a living Imam as an authoritative interpreter — the Syrian debater was ultimately unable to counter this argument and embraced the Shia doctrine of Imamate. At the end, the Imam evaluated each debater's methodology: praising Humran for following narrations, gently criticizing others for mixing truth with analogical reasoning, and expressing the highest praise for the young Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who argued with such skill that even the Imam himself approved.
